sentences.text:
Shri Atul E. R. Jaiswal, learned counsel for the ap  Shri Bhashkar Agrawal, advocate appearing on behalf  Kumar Gupta, learned counsel for the respondent.
 Shri Sanjay Patwa, learned counsel for the responde  ORDER
This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 20.12.2006 passed in claim case No.46/2006 challenging the quantum of compensation.

2. The owner i.e. respondent No.1 has also filed his cross-objection in this appeal thereby disputing its liability by asserting that the registration was subsequently renewed, thus, the expiry of registration and its renewal would only constitute a mere irregularity which would not absolve the insurance company from its liability to pay compensation.

3. The short facts of the case are that on 03.02.2025 the appellant Sheerkhan was going along with his daughter-in-law on motor cycle bearing 2 MA-1330-2007 registration number MP09-JB-0564,
when they reached near Mari Maata Square, Indore, a scooter bearing registration number MP09-WG-0870, which was being ridden by the respondent No.1 in a rash and negligent manner,
dashed into the motor cycle of Sheerkhan which resulted in grievous injuries to both of them.
4. The appellant/Sheerkhan filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him.

The claims tribunal after recording evidence awarded total compensation to the tune of Rs.28000/- to the appellant, however, while awarding such compensation, the insurance company was exonerated from its liability to pay compensation on the ground that the registration certificate has already expired in the year 2000,
thus, there was no valid registration consequently no subsisting contract of insurance, hence,
insurance company is not liable to pay compensation.

5. Learned counsel for the claimants submits that the claims tribunal while considering the compensation has completely ignored the fact that the appellant has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 23%, however, a meager amount of Rs.28000/- has been awarded by holding in terms of para 14 of the award that the income of the appellant has increased which shows that the Sheerkhan vs Ramesh Chandra on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108528688/
1 permanent disability has not resulted in loss of earning capacity.
Hence, nothing has been awarded for permanent disability.

He submits that the claims tribunal has erred in concluding so, for the reason that it is not the question of loss of earning capacity in abstract, however, it is the loss of capacity to increase the income which is relevant in the present case.
He 3 MA-1330-2007 submits that although the appellant earned Rs.10,000/- on the date of deposition before the tribunal in comparison to Rs.8000/- on the date of accident.
However, there may have been a case where he could have increased his income more than Rs.10,000/-, had he not suffered with the permanent disability sustained in the accident.
Thus, he submits that the compensation for sustaining permanent disability should have been awarded by the claims tribunal.

6. Learned counsel for the owner i.e. respondent No.1 submits that the claims tribunal while awarding compensation has exonerated the insurance company by holding in terms of para 17 of the award that the registration of the vehicle was for 15 years in terms of provisions of section 41 sub-section 7 of the Motor Vehicles Act which expired in the year 2000 because the vehicle got registered in the year of 1985 as would be apparent from Ex.D-1, thus, in absence of renewal of the registration there was no subsisting contract of insurance, hence, the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation.

He submits that this finding of the claims tribunal is erroneous inasmuch as the non renewal of the registration certificate was merely an irregularity which could have been corrected by the owner of the vehicle at any given point of time.

This question was considered by the Jurisdictional High Court of Kerala in the case of Joby Thomas & Another v.
Annamma Augustine & Another, 2012 ACJ, 848 and after considering the provisions of Section 149 and 192 r/w Section 39 of the Motor Vehicles Act, the Court held that renewal of the registration certificate would entail that the insurance company is liable to pay compensation.

sentences.text: In the present case also, in 4 MA-1330-2007 the year of 2007, the registration certificate was renewed, hence, in the present case also the insurance company is liable to pay compensation.
He further relies on judgment of Karnataka High Court, and Punjab and Haryana High Court in this regard.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurance company controverting submissions of both the counsels submits that in view of the clear findings recorded by the claims tribunal in para 9 and 14 of the impugned award, it is clear that there was no loss of earning capacity of the claimant/appellant, hence, the claims tribunal has correctly awarded an amount of Rs.28000/- in other heads.

As far as the liability of the insurance company is concerned, he points out the provisions of Chapter 4 of the Motor Vehicles Act particularly Section 39 and 41 (7, 8, 10 and 11) of the Act and submits that the absence of renewal would mean that there is no vehicle in existence in the eye of law and consequently, the term that is life time of the vehicle got determined on the expiry of the registration.
Thus, the findings of the claims tribunal in this regard are correct, hence, no interference is warranted.
8. Learned counsel for the insurance company has further argued that the cross objection has been filed by the owner/respondent No.1 against the co- respondent which is not maintainable.
He further submits that proper appeal by paying not only due court fees but also statutory amount in terms of the proviso to Section 173 should have been filed by the owner.
Hence, on this ground alone the cross objection deserves to be dismissed.

2 9.

In rejoinder submissions, the counsel for the owner/respondent No.1 submits that he has already deposited 50% of the awarded amount, thus, he 5 MA-1330-2007 has already complied with the requirement of deposit of statutory amount in terms of Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, hence,
on this ground the cross-objection should not be dismissed.

He further submits that there is no stipulation in insurance policy regarding the currency of contract of insurance till the subsistence of registration certificate and the policy was never cancelled by the insurance company.

10. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
11.
On perusal of the record it is seen that Ex.D-1 is the policy of the vehicle.
Certainly, the provision of Chapter 4 of the Motor Vehicles Act provides for necessity of registration of the vehicle.
Section 41 provides for manner and method of registration of the vehicle.
In Sub-section 7, it is provided that maximum period for subsistence of registration of vehicle is 15 years and then there is stipulation of its renewal for further period of 5 years.

12. In the present case, the vehicle in question i.e. scooter was initially registered in the year of 1985 which completed its 15 years in the year of 2000 whereafter there was no renewal of registration of the vehicle.

The vehicle met with an accident on 03.02.2005 and only thereafter the owner woke up to the need of renewal of registration and got it renewed in the year 2007 i.e. on 03.08.2007 which was for further period of 5 years i.e. upto 02.08.2012.
When an insurance company enters into an agreement with the owner of a vehicle for indemnifying in the eventuality as provided under Section 147/149 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

The expectation in respect of the term/tenure of the policy in a case of an insurance policy of the nature involved in the instant case would be for the life of the insured vehicle i.e. 6 MA-1330-2007 statutory life time of the vehicle which in terms of Section 41 is 15 years with a stipulation of renewal of further 5 years.

13. In the considered view of this Court the date on which the accident occurred there was no renewal of the registration, thus, there was no subsisting contract of insurance between the owner and the insurer on the date of the accident.
As regards the case as relied upon by the learned counsel, it is seen that in all three cases the expiry and renewal of the vehicle was within a very short span of time.

In the case of Punjab and Haryana High Court, the registration expired on 15.03.2014 and vehicle was renewed on 10.02.2015 whereas in the present case, renewal was after more than 7 years of the expiry of the registration, which is beyond even the renewal period of 5 years.
Hence, in the considered view of this Court, the tribunal has not erred in exonerating the insurance company from liability from payment of compensation.

As regards the question of enhancement, it is indeed correct that 23% Permanent Disability must have affected the progression of the claimant/appellant in his career looking to the nature of work which he was doing.

As such not awarding anything to the claimant for sustaining permanent disability to the extent of 23% is not proper, however, looking to the long pendency of the present case i.e. it relates to the year of 2007, this Court is not inclined to remand the matter back to the tribunal for quantification of compensation for sustaining permanent disability.
As such, further sum of Rs.30,000/- in lump-sum is awarded.
In the considered view of this Court, this amount together with the amount earlier awarded by the claims tribunal will constitute a just compensation in the case.
This amount 7 MA-1330-2007 of Rs.30,000/- shall carry interest @6% per annum from the date of the application before the claims tribunal.

3 14. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed of.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
